newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Apr 21.

text.p: Board admits 'screw-up' on butter: The New Zealand Dairy Board admitted on Sunday night that it had not paid the right levies on butter imported into Europe, but said there had been no intent to defraud. Page 1.

Coalition ministers get minders: The government, dogged by damaging slip-ups that are taking their toll in the opinion polls, is introducing a ministerial minder system in a bid to get a tighter, more united performance as Parliament resumes tomorrow. Page 1.
Cabinet may postpone till next Monday a decision to proceed with the planned $94 million ministerial building, dubbed a "palace" by ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble. Page 2.

Conference off till October: Delaying the government's population conference till October will provide time for research on immigration and population issues, Immigration Minister Max Bradford said. Page 2.
Don't harm government - PM: Prime Minister Jim Bolger has urged National Party members not to upset the government by trying to distinguish the party from coalition partner NZ First. Page 2.
Trade dispute with Iran 'over': The trade dispute with Iran was over, a spokesman for Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Sunday. Page 2.

Labour won't be bound by 'shonky' super poll: Future Labour governments would not be bound by the outcome of a "shonky" referendum on compulsory superannuation, according to Labour deputy leader Michael Cullen. Page 2.
Gay couples face exclusion: Justice Minister Doug Graham confirmed on Sunday that homosexual couples were likely to be excluded from amendments to the Matrimonial Property Act. Page 2.

NZ leads world in use of eftpos transactions: Eftpos use in New Zealand has continued to climb, with 200 million transactions in 1996, an increase of about 25 percent, Bankers Association figures show. Page 11.
TV3 provides more revenue: Canwest increased revenue from its 68 percent stake in TV3 by more than 100 percent for the six months to February compared to the six months to February 1996. Page 11.
Rail yards sooner: Tranz Rail believes it can reduce construction time for its $28 million freight yards project at Middleton in Christchurch from three to two years. Page 13.
Help for Heritage: Mineral exploration company Heritage Mining expects to form at least one joint venture this year to search for gold in the Coromandel. Page 13.
